newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 26.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 26.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open on Thursday, despite the fury of Tropical Storm Carlos off the Pacific Coast, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.

Carlos was spotted early Thursday at 45 miles (72 km) west-southwest of the Socorro island and moving at 10 knots (19 km/11 miles per hour) with winds from 45 to 55 knots (85 to 104 km/50 to 61 miles per hour). Waves 12 feet high at a radius of about 50 miles.

The storm is expected to continue west-northwest in the next 24 hours, the bulletin said. It warned ships from sailing around the Revillagigedo islands, about 600 km/375 miles west of Mexico's Pacific coast.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
Tropical Storm Carlos dropping rain along Colima, Sinaloa, Nayarit, Jalisco, Michoacan and Chiapas states. The depression was located about 140 miles (224 km) from the coast and moving northwest.
Clear skies and hot temperatures along the remainder of the coastline with maximum winds 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour) and waves three to six feet high.

Light isolated rains expected later in the day along coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco and Campeche states. Generally clear skies and maximum winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour).
Cloudy and rains along coasts of Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Quintana Roo, Belize and the Yucatan peninsula.
Winds from 10 to 15 knots and waves three to five feet high.

Two storm fronts spotten in the region, one off the coast of Colombia moving west at 10 to 15 knots and the other off the coast of Venezuela, moving west at between 15 and 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles).
